frus-1864p3:
France leads Part III of the 1864 foreign affairs papers. The French legation's letters follow the main French file. Russia, the Netherlands, China, and Japan complete the volume. Dayton in Paris reports warships building for the Confederacy. The Florida lies at Brest. Ironclads rise at Bordeaux and Nantes. Seward protests each hull in turn.

Mexico runs beside the ship cases. France's Mexican venture shadows every exchange with Paris. The Rappahannock case recurs through the winter letters. Russian papers carry a warmer tone. One letter thanks America for the fleet visit's welcome. The Japan file extends the story to the Pacific. Civil War diplomacy here spans three oceans.
frus-1865p3:
Part III of the 1865 papers sweeps the smaller courts of Europe and beyond. Austria opens the file, with Prussia and Belgium behind. Portugal, Italy, and Rome follow. Denmark, Sweden, and Switzerland have sections. Japan, Turkey, Egypt, and the Barbary states extend the range. Mexico then takes the largest share of the volume.

The Mexico papers dominate by weight. A long run comes from the French legation. Austrian and European troops for Mexico get their own headings. Washington watches the French empire in Mexico with open hostility. The Austrian file adds its own color. Motley reports Richmond's fall and Europe's shock at Lincoln's death. One volume thus joins two stories. Europe's condolences meet America's next quarrel.
frus-1866p3:
Mexico dominates Part III of the 1866 papers. The main file follows a new American envoy, Campbell. Seward sends him to reach President Juarez. French troops are leaving Mexico that autumn. Maximilian decides to stay and issues a December proclamation. Campbell sails with General Sherman on the Susquehanna. His letters report delays at Havana and talks with exiles.

The Mexican legation's papers form the second block. Venezuela and Colombia close the volume. A legation analysis argues that Maximilian's own friends doubt his title. It calls his planned vote an admission of weakness. These papers catch an empire in collapse. Washington backs the republic while France withdraws. The volume is the fullest Mexico record of the year.
